name: Geolocation
plain: Asks the person for their device location, precise or approximate.
meaning: Tells the site where the person physically is, down to a few meters outdoors: home, workplace, travel, daily routine. Repeated fixes reveal patterns of life.

web.api: navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(), watchPosition(), clearWatch(); options enableHighAccuracy, timeout, maximumAge

access.prompt_ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow while visiting, Allow this time (Chrome 116), Don't allow. Firefox: Allow or Block with optional Remember. Safari: Allow or Don't Allow. Android 12+: Precise or Approximate choice. OS Location Services must also be on.
access.persistence: Chrome and Edge: persistent per origin after Allow; Allow this time ends when the tab closes or is backgrounded. Firefox: permanent only if Remember is ticked. Safari: asks again per visit unless set to Allow.
access.revocation: Padlock and Site settings; Chrome Safety Check auto-resets unused permissions; PermissionStatus 'change' event; turning off OS Location Services blocks all sites.
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes need allow="geolocation"; the decision is keyed to the top-level origin.
steps: Browser checks Permissions Policy and secure context
Browser shows prompt unless a decision is stored
OS provider (GPS, Wi-Fi, cell, IP) returns a fix
Success callback gets GeolocationPosition, or error callback gets code 1 PERMISSION_DENIED, 2 POSITION_UNAVAILABLE, 3 TIMEOUT

chrome_android.note: Android 12+ lets the person choose Approximate (about 2 km square) or Precise

data.metric: Coordinates with accuracy radius and optional speed and heading
data.update: one-shot, or continuous via watchPosition (about 1 update per second on GPS)

fields.name: accuracy
fields.precision: typical 5 to 20 m GPS, 20 to 100 m Wi-Fi, 1 to 5 km cell or IP

fields.name: maximumAge
fields.precision: cached fix up to this age is accepted

limits.headline: Can find where your device is, once or while the page is open
limits.user_action: You tap Use my location, Find stores near me or a map button, then choose Allow
can: Find your position, precise or approximate where the device lets you choose
Check your position again while the page stays open
Remember your answer if you choose Allow while visiting or Remember
cannot: Track you in the background while the page is closed
Use your location after you pick Don't allow or after one time access ends
Get a precise spot if you choose approximate on Android 12 or later
Skip the prompt, which always asks first on a new site
limits.differs: Chrome offers Allow this time. Android 12 and later lets you pick precise or approximate. Safari and Firefox offer Allow or Don't Allow with an optional remember.

story.what_it_is: A site asks where you physically are.

marketing.name: Geolocation API
marketing.pitch: Describes the permission that lets a site ask for your location, with a prompt you can allow or block.

marketing.name: User location
marketing.pitch: Google teaches developers how to ask for and use a person's location on the web.

story.for_you: A prompt says 'Allow this site to know your location?' You choose Allow once, Allow while using, or Block. If you allow, the site may see you within meters. It can also check again later.
story.for_makers: Location powers maps, nearby results and delivery. It lets makers show local prices, stores and weather. It is also valuable for ads and for proving you are in an allowed place, such as a legal betting region.

use_cases.example: A web map centers on your blue dot and gives directions from where you are.
A food site shows only restaurants that deliver to your spot.
A location based web game or geocaching page shows treasures near you.
A betting or fantasy site checks that you are inside a state where play is legal before it lets you bet.
A ride web page sets your pickup point to where you stand.
A store site shows the nearest pickup store and stock.
A bank may check that a login location fits your normal area.
An ad network uses repeated fixes to learn your home, work and routine.

technical_bounds: No location without a visible prompt or a stored grant
No background geolocation after the tab closes
Mobile browsers pause or throttle updates in background tabs
Desktop without GPS returns Wi-Fi or IP estimates (20 m to 5 km)
Blocked in insecure contexts and in cross-origin iframes without allow

abuse: Home and workplace inference from repeated fixes
Selling movement data through ad SDKs
Prompt spam on load to wear users down

history.change: iOS 14 adds system Precise Location toggle that applies to Safari websites
Approximate vs Precise choice added to the Android location dialog
One-time permission (Allow this time) added for geolocation, camera, microphone
Browser-drawn <geolocation> element ships as an alternative request path
